sources.title: Yoav Benjamini and Daniel Yekutieli, The Control of the False Discovery Rate in Multiple Testing under Dependency, The Annals of Statistics 29(4) (2001)
sources.locator: Author-uploaded full 24-page article. Inspected the PRDS definition and distinctions in Section 2.2 (PDF pp. 4–5), Theorem 1.2 and its complete Section 4 proof (PDF pp. 4, 13–16), and Theorem 1.3 with the complete Section 5 harmonic-correction argument (PDF pp. 5, 18–19). Also checked the two-sided and pairwise-comparison caveats in Section 4 (PDF pp. 17–18). The local BY proof strengthens the source route to all superuniform null p-values by replacing its uniform interval-mass step with a CDF summation-by-parts argument.

alternatives.argument: Define the finite step-up rule directly from the published harmonic number H_m and critical values kq/(mH_m); the procedure and threshold domain are fully stated in the local algorithm item.

State PRDS as monotonicity of regular conditional probabilities of increasing Borel sets on the true-null coordinate support. The local definition names the standard-Borel target, AC-bearing RCD existence, factorization to conditioning values, support convention, and kernel version.

For any nondecreasing cutoff sequence, define C_i,k by the remaining order statistics. The local proof establishes the exact rejection-count event, Borel measurability, disjoint cover, and increasing cumulative sets, including m=1 and boundary ranks.

Expand FDR by true-null index and rejection count; use the local step-up partition, divide the p_i range into intervals of width t=q/(mH_m), bound the weighted interval sum using the validity CDF F_j<=jt and finite summation by parts, then sum q/m over the true-null indices. This proves the claimed superuniform discrete scope without a dependence assumption.

Use the generic step-up partition, superuniformity, and the PRDS conditional monotonicity of the nested increasing events D_i,k to fold the rejection-count contributions into a sum at most q/m for each true-null coordinate. The complete proof handles zero conditioning-event probabilities and the final whole-space event.

Sum the locally proved per-null contribution bound over the fixed true-null set to obtain FDR<=m_0 q/m<=q. The theorem preserves the exact PRDS premise and carries its AC-bearing conditional-law branch.

Give a four-state two-pvalue experiment with superuniform marginals and covariance 28/625>0; for the increasing event {p_2>=4/5}, the forced conditional probabilities at p_1=3/5 and 4/5 are 1 and 0, so PRDS fails.

sources.title: Alexandru Katsevich, STAT 9610: Statistical Learning and High-Dimensional Statistics, full course lecture notes
sources.locator: Full 146-page course notes; inspected Chapter 6.3.2, PDF pp. 136–139. Pages 136–137 define valid p-values, FDP/FDR and BH; pages 138–139 give the harmonic BY calculation and PRDS theorem context. Its interval-mass bound is used here only for exact-uniform null p-values; the local proof supplies the wider discrete-superuniform scope by CDF summation by parts.
